identity.title: InfoTok: Adaptive Discrete Video Tokenizer via Information-Theoretic Compression

problem.claim: The paper addresses accurate and efficient discrete video tokenization for processing long video sequences.

gap.claim: Current tokenizers compress all video content at a fixed rate despite variable information density, causing redundancy or information loss.

contributions.claim: Introduces an information-theoretic framework for adaptive video tokenization.
Reports a proof that existing data-agnostic training methods are suboptimal in representation length and presents an ELBO-based algorithm intended to approach theoretical optimality.
Develops a transformer-based adaptive compressor that implements adaptive tokenization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach as a principled, information-theoretic framework with a novel ELBO-based adaptive tokenization algorithm and transformer compressor.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art compression performance, including 20% token savings without performance influence.
The authors report achieving 2.3× compression rates while outperforming prior heuristic adaptive approaches.
The authors report a theoretical result that existing data-agnostic training methods are suboptimal in representation length.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-video processing requires accurate and efficient discrete video tokenization.
Fixed-rate compression fails to reflect videos’ variable information density, producing redundancy or information loss.
The paper proposes an information-theoretic adaptive framework, an ELBO-based algorithm, and a transformer compressor.
The authors report token savings and stronger compression performance than prior heuristic adaptive methods.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links variable information density to fixed-rate compression, then motivates allocating tokens according to informational richness.

lessons.interpretation: Making the failure mode structurally match the proposed allocation rule gives the method rationale a direct problem-to-design connection.
lessons.application: When presenting an adaptive representation method, explicitly map the measured or hypothesized source variability to the mechanism that changes resource allocation.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the task requires uniform-rate representations or when information density cannot be operationalized reliably.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, evaluation tasks, baselines, or conditions behind the reported compression and performance figures.
The abstract does not define how informational richness, performance influence, or theoretical optimality are measured.
The symbol used for the proposed method is unresolved in the abstract text, although the paper title identifies InfoTok.
